pages.title: Axiom Schema
pages.text: The starting assumptions of a system, written out as patterns that stand for infinitely many individual axioms. Change one and you change what can be proved. The slate is plain and heavy, and every line carved on it is accepted without proof.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found my first schemas in Euclid's vault and among the debris of Axiom Sentinels. Building my own meant encoding natural number rules into a qubit until the Formal Proof Assistant would accept them as given.
